## Why This Is Asked

Tests real-world risk scenarios for policy changes in multi-tenant Vault Enterprise deployments. A canary rollout exercises isolation, policy versioning, and lease-audit workflows before broad rollout.

## Key Concepts

- Canary rollout in per-tenant namespaces
- AppRole-to-policy bindings
- TTL hardening and revocation flows
- Audit log verification and rollback safety

## Code Example

```bash
# Create canary policy in canary namespace
vault policy write tenant-approvals-canary - <<EOF
path "auth/approle/role/tenant-*/token_ttl" {
  capabilities = ["update"]
}
EOF

# Bind AppRoles to canary policy (per tenant)
vault write auth/approle/role/tenant-a-approle policies=tenant-approvals-canary
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you automate tenant selection and progressive rollout?
- What metrics indicate safe promotion or failure?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This evaluates practical implementation of Vault's SSH secret engine in multi-tenant environments, focusing on security isolation, operational continuity, and proper handling of cryptographic rotations.

## Key Concepts
- Namespace-based tenant isolation in Vault Enterprise
- SSH certificate lifecycle management with ephemeral credentials
- Host key rotation strategies preserving session continuity
- Lease-based revocation and immediate access termination
- Cross-tenant isolation validation techniques
- Rolling deployment patterns for zero-downtime updates

## Code Example
```bash
# Create per-tenant SSH role
vault write ssh/roles/tenant1-jump \
  ttl=24h \
  max_ttl=24h \
  allowed_users="jumpuser" \
  allow_user_certificates=true \
  key_type="ca" \
  default_critical_options=["no-port-forwarding"] \
  default_extensions=["permit-X11-forwarding"]

# Sign SSH certificate for tenant user
vault write -field=signed_key ssh/sign/tenant1-jump \
  public_key=@/home/jumpuser/.ssh/id_rsa.pub \
  valid_principals=jumpuser \
  ttl=8h

# Revoke all tenant leases immediately
vault lease revoke -prefix ssh/creds/tenant1-jump

# Clean up tenant configuration
vault delete ssh/roles/tenant1-jump

# Host key rotation (conceptual)
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key -N ""
vault write ssh/config/ca host_key=@/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub
```

## Code Example

```
vault write transit/keys/tenant-<id> type="aes256-gcm96"

```

- How do you ensure data-at-rest integrity during rotation in multi-service deployments?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests namespace isolation, policy scoping, AppRole bindings, and audit/rollback in Vault Enterprise. It ensures hands-on ability to set up tenant boundaries, credentials, and observability.

## Key Concepts
- Vault namespaces and per-tenant isolation
- KV v2 secret engine paths and read permissions
- Policy scoping to tenant data
- AppRole binding to a tenant policy
- Basic auditing and rollback procedures

## Code Example
```bash
vault namespace create tenant-a
vault secrets enable -path=secret kv-v2
vault policy write tenant-a-read - <<'EOF'
path "secret/data/tenant-a/*" { capabilities = ["read"] }
EOF
vault write auth/approle/role/tenant-a-app token_ttl=20m token_max_ttl=1h policies=tenant-a-read
ROLE_ID=$(vault read -field=role_id auth/approle/role/tenant-a-app/role-id)
SECRET_ID=$(vault write -f -field=secret_id auth/approle/role/tenant-a-app/secret-id)
vault login -method=approle role_id="$ROLE_ID" secret_id="$SECRET_ID"
vault kv get secret/data/tenant-a/config
vault audit enable file /var/log/vault_audit.log
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you verify isolation across multiple tenants after onboarding?
- What changes would you make to support tenant offboarding cleanly?
- How would you test under a simulated audit load without affecting production?

Tests practical use of Vault SSH secrets for controlled, time-bound access with tenant isolation and automated revocation.

- SSH secret engine basics
- Per-tenant namespaces and role-scoped policies
- TTLs and lease revocation

```bash
path "ssh/creds/tenant-<id>-ssh" { capabilities = ["read"] }

```
